title: Chatbots for Enterprise Selling: 2026 Buyer's Guide
summary: 11 B2B sales chatbots and AI website agents compared on qualification, routing, meeting booking and CRM sync, with pricing checked by Storylane.
body_markdown:
If you run demand gen, product marketing or the website at a B2B company, the chatbot you pick has one job: turn the right visitors into qualified meetings without making the wrong ones wait for a human. Most tools sold as "AI chatbots for sales" are built for something else, usually support deflection, and that difference only shows up after you have signed.


The short answer: there is no single best AI chatbot for B2B sales. Your CRM, your traffic volume and how your buyers like to evaluate a product decide it. Salesforce shops running account-based inbound tend to land on Qualified (now part of Salesforce) or Agentforce. HubSpot teams should start with HubSpot's own tools. Teams whose bottleneck is speed to meeting look at Chili Piper. Teams who want the agent to answer detailed product questions and show the product inside the conversation look at tools like Storylane RepX (that is us).


Below: how to tell a sales chatbot apart from a support bot and from an AI website agent, the six things that matter for B2B, and each tool checked against its own website in October 2026.


## Sales chatbot, support bot or AI website agent: which one do you need?


Three kinds of product get sold under the same "AI chatbot" label. They are measured differently, trained on different material and hand off to different people.


Type Job Success metric Hands off to Typical examples


Rule-based sales chatbot Capture and route visitors through scripted, branching flows Leads captured, meetings booked SDR or AE HubSpot chatbot builder, classic Drift playbooks


Support bot Answer questions so a human does not have to Resolution or deflection rate Support agent Intercom Fin, Tidio Lyro


AI website agent (AI SDR) Hold an open conversation, answer product questions, qualify against your ICP, book or route Qualified conversations, meetings, pipeline The account owner, with the transcript Qualified Piper, Warmly, 1mind, Storylane RepX


The quickest test: ask a vendor what number their customers report. If the answer is a resolution or deflection rate, you are looking at a support tool. A "resolved" conversation can be a prospect who got an answer and left without talking to sales. For the longer version of this distinction, see[chatbots vs AI agents and how to choose](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chatbots-vs-ai-agents) .


## What actually matters for B2B


Feature lists are nearly identical across vendors. These six things are where tools really differ, and each one can be tested in a trial.


### 1. Qualification against your ICP


The bot should ask a short set of questions that adapt to what the visitor already said, and use what it knows about the company (size, industry, target-account status) so it does not ask what you already know. Check whether you define the rules in plain language or have to build a decision tree, and whether you can set different rules per page. More on how this works in[real-time lead qualification](https://www.storylane.io/blog/real-time-lead-qualification) .


### 2. Routing to the right owner


A qualified visitor from a named account should reach that account's owner, not a round-robin queue. Ask how the tool reads ownership (from your CRM in real time, or from its own copy of the rules) and what happens when the owner is offline.


### 3. Meeting booking in the conversation


The visitor should see a calendar while they are still on the page. Check whether scheduling is built in or needs a separate tool (Chili Piper, Calendly, HubSpot meetings), because that is an extra contract and an extra place for routing rules to drift apart.


### 4. CRM sync you can inspect


Ask which objects and fields the tool writes, whether it creates or updates records (and how it handles duplicates), and whether the sync is real time or batched. "Integrates with Salesforce" can mean a native app, a Zapier recipe or a webhook you have to maintain. All three can work; you just need to know which one you are buying. If you are not on HubSpot, our guide to[website AI agents for Salesforce, Pipedrive or a custom CRM](https://www.storylane.io/blog/website-ai-agent-salesforce-pipedrive-crm) lists what to check.


### 5. Handoff to a human


Test it yourself: pose as a high-intent buyer, ask to talk to sales, and time how long it takes, who you reach and how much they already know. A rep who opens the conversation without the transcript makes the visitor repeat themselves at the exact moment they were ready to buy.


### 6. Accuracy on product questions


This is where AI agents beat scripted bots and where they can also do damage. Feed the tool your docs and pricing page, then ask it the ten hardest questions your sales team gets, including ones it should refuse (custom pricing, roadmap, security commitments). Check what sources it learns from, whether you can review and correct answers, and whether it says "I don't know" rather than guessing. Ask whether conversation data is used to train shared models; our post on[AI website agents and data privacy](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-agents-data-privacy-b2b) covers the questions procurement will ask.


## The tools, checked on their own sites (October 2026)


Every pricing model below was read from the vendor's own website on October 23, 2026. "Quote-based" means the vendor does not publish a price. Prices change, so treat these as a starting point for your own quote.


Tool Type Best fit Pricing model Key consideration


Qualified (Piper) AI website agent Salesforce shops running account-based inbound Quote-based (Premier, Enterprise, Ultimate) Center of gravity is Salesforce; now part of Salesforce


Salesforce Agentforce AI agent platform Teams already deep in Salesforce Published: $2 per conversation, or Flex Credits Built for Salesforce orgs; you configure the agent yourself


HubSpot chatbot builder Rule-based chatbot Teams on HubSpot CRM starting out Free, with premium features in paid Hubs Scripted flows, not open conversation


Warmly Visitor identification + AI chat Signal-led inbound on identified accounts Published: Inbound Chat $20,000/yr; AI Inbound Autopilot $30,000/yr Only as good as your ICP filters


ZoomInfo Chat Data-enriched chat Existing ZoomInfo customers Quote-based Hard to justify without the wider ZoomInfo contract


Chili Piper Routing and scheduling (with chat) High-volume inbound where speed to meeting is the bottleneck Published: from $1,250/mo, billed annually Strongest at booking, lighter on open-ended product Q&A


Conversica AI agents across email, SMS and chat Following up and reviving leads at scale Quote-based Strength is follow-up, not on-page conversation


Drift / 1mind Legacy chatbot / AI agent Existing Drift customers planning a move Quote-based Salesloft says it has transitioned from Drift to 1mind


Intercom Fin Support AI agent Support-heavy teams Published: $0.99 per outcome, plus helpdesk seats Measured on resolutions, not pipeline


Tidio Support chat + Lyro AI Small teams and ecommerce Free plan; paid from $24.17/mo; Lyro from $32.50/mo Little B2B qualification or routing depth


Storylane RepX AI website agent with interactive demos Teams whose buyers want to see the product before a call Free up to 2K visitors/mo; from $24K/yr Shows the real product inside the conversation


### Qualified (Piper)


Piper is Qualified's AI SDR agent. It talks to website visitors by text, voice or video, books meetings and routes conversations, with account segmentation and enrichment included in every plan. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Qualified on April 1, 2026, and says the capabilities are being brought into Agentforce. All three plans (Premier, Enterprise, Ultimate) are quote-based and sized by monthly web sessions; handoff to a live agent appears from the Enterprise plan up. Pick it if Salesforce is your system of record and you run account-based inbound. If you are not on Salesforce, much of its advantage goes away, and the product roadmap now sits inside Salesforce's.


### Salesforce Agentforce


Agentforce is Salesforce's platform for building AI agents, including agents that greet website visitors, answer questions and book meetings for sellers. Salesforce publishes its pricing: $2 per conversation for customer-facing agents, or Flex Credits at $500 per 100,000 credits. It inherits everything your org already knows about an account. The trade-off is effort: you are configuring a platform, not switching on a finished website agent, and it only makes sense if you already run on Salesforce.


### HubSpot


HubSpot's chatbot builder is free and writes straight to the same contact records your reps use, so there is no sync to break. The bots are scripted flows, with more advanced features in the paid Marketing, Sales and Service Hubs; HubSpot also sells a separate AI customer agent. It is the sensible first step for a HubSpot team, and the right question is when a scripted bot stops being enough. We cover that in[HubSpot chatbot vs an AI sales agent](https://www.storylane.io/blog/hubspot-chatbot-vs-ai-sales-agent) .


### Warmly


Warmly identifies companies and people visiting your site, then alerts reps, routes leads and (on its chat plans) engages visitors with an AI chatbot. Pricing is published: web de-anonymization at $10,000 a year, Inbound Chat at $20,000 a year and AI Inbound Autopilot at $30,000 a year, billed annually. It suits teams that want reps acting on known accounts in the moment. Identification data is only useful if it matches your target segment, so tune your ICP filters during the trial before you judge the alerts.


### ZoomInfo Chat


ZoomInfo Chat combines live chat, a chatbot and a meeting scheduler with ZoomInfo's company data, so it can route on revenue, size and location. Pricing is not published. It is a natural add-on if you already pay for ZoomInfo data and a harder case as a standalone chat purchase.


### Chili Piper


Chili Piper's core is qualifying, routing and scheduling inbound leads from forms and handoffs, with instant calls from forms and a "Chat AI" capability for 24/7 engagement. Pricing is published and annual only: Routing & Scheduling at $1,250 a month (15 seats) and Experiences at $3,500 a month (30 seats). Confirm which plan includes Chat AI before you compare it to a dedicated agent. Pick it when the leak is the gap between "interested" and "meeting booked". If you are weighing chat-first options, see[Chili Piper Chat alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-chat-alternatives) .


### Conversica


Conversica sells AI agents that hold conversations over email, SMS, chat and messaging apps, for acquisition, support and retention. Pricing is not published. Its strength is persistent follow-up with leads your team never got to, so treat it as a layer beside your website agent rather than the website agent itself.


### Drift and 1mind


Drift set the template for conversational marketing. Salesloft's Drift page now says "We've transitioned from Drift to 1mind", and 1mind sells AI agents for website inbound, live sales calls and in-product guidance, with no public pricing. Do not start a new Drift deployment in 2026. If you are on Drift today, use this year to plan the move; our list of[Drift alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-alternatives) is a starting point.


### Intercom Fin


Fin is a strong support agent. Intercom prices it at $0.99 per outcome, plus helpdesk seats (Essential lists at $29 per seat per month, shown discounted for new customers when we checked), and it can also run on top of other helpdesks. Buy it to answer customers. Do not expect it to report pipeline, and model the per-outcome cost at your real volume, because a more useful bot costs more each month.


### Tidio


Tidio pairs live chat with its Lyro AI agent. There is a free plan, Starter from $24.17 a month and Growth from $49.17 a month, with Lyro sold from $32.50 a month for 50 AI conversations. It is quick to set up and cheap to test. It is built for support and ecommerce, so you will outgrow it once qualification and routing to named owners matter.


### Storylane RepX (full disclosure: this is us)


[RepX](https://www.storylane.io/repx) is Storylane's AI agent for your website. It talks to visitors by text, voice or video, asks discovery questions, qualifies them against ICP rules you write in plain English, books meetings, and can open an interactive demo inside the conversation so the visitor sees the feature they asked about. You train it on your website, docs, sales call transcripts, demos, slides and videos. Storylane's site lists it as free for up to 2,000 visitors a month and from $24K a year with Demo Suite and scheduling included.


Qualified leads and conversation summaries flow to HubSpot, Salesforce and Slack.


## Who should pick what


- **Salesforce is your CRM and you run account-based inbound:** Qualified or Agentforce. Native depth matters more than price at this point.
- **HubSpot is your CRM and you are starting out:** HubSpot's free chatbot builder, then an AI agent with native HubSpot sync once scripted flows stop keeping up.
- **Your problem is speed to meeting on forms:** Chili Piper.
- **You want reps working identified accounts in real time:** Warmly, or ZoomInfo Chat if you already buy ZoomInfo.
- **Your buyers ask detailed product questions before they will book:** an AI website agent that can show the product, such as RepX.
- **Your goal is fewer support tickets:** Intercom Fin or Tidio. Different job, different metric.
- **You are on Drift:** plan the migration now rather than at renewal.


## How to run a trial that tells you something


1. Pick one or two high-intent pages (pricing, a product page) rather than the whole site, so the conversations are worth reading.
2. Write the qualification rules and the owner-routing rules down before you configure anything, and connect the CRM in a test environment first.
3. Ask the bot your sales team's hardest questions, including ones it should decline, and correct its answers before it goes live.
4. Decide the metric up front: qualified conversations and meetings booked from those pages, compared with the same pages before the trial. Chat volume tells you nothing.
5. Read the transcripts every week. They show what the dashboard hides: wrong answers, missed handoffs and questions your website does not answer.


On pricing, ask every vendor for a quote at your projected twelve-month traffic, including overage and seats. Per-outcome and per-conversation models are cheap at low volume and grow with usage; so a bot that gets more useful also gets more expensive.


## FAQ


### What is the best AI chatbot for B2B sales teams?


It depends on your CRM and how your buyers evaluate. Qualified and Agentforce fit Salesforce-centric account-based teams, HubSpot's tools fit HubSpot teams starting out, Chili Piper fits teams focused on speed to meeting, and AI website agents like Storylane RepX fit buyers who want product answers and a demo before a call. Judge each on qualified meetings, not chat volume.


### What is the difference between a sales chatbot and an AI sales agent?


A traditional sales chatbot follows scripted, branching flows. An AI sales agent holds an open conversation, answers questions from your content, qualifies against rules you set and books or routes the visitor. Agents handle questions a script did not anticipate, which also means you need to check their accuracy.


### Can one bot handle both sales and support?


It can, but the two jobs pull in opposite directions: support bots aim to resolve without a human, sales bots aim to get the right human involved quickly. Many B2B teams run a support agent in the product and help center and a sales agent on high-intent marketing pages.


### Do AI sales chatbots integrate with Salesforce and HubSpot?


Most do, but depth varies. Some are native apps that read ownership and write fields in real time; others connect through Zapier or webhooks. Ask each vendor which objects and fields it writes and whether the sync is real time. For example, Storylane RepX sends qualified leads and conversation summaries to HubSpot, Salesforce and Slack.


### How much does a B2B sales chatbot cost?


From free (HubSpot's chatbot builder, Tidio's free plan) to tens of thousands of dollars a year. Published examples as of October 2026: Chili Piper from $1,250 a month billed annually, Warmly's Inbound Chat at $20,000 a year, Agentforce at $2 per conversation. Qualified, ZoomInfo Chat, Conversica and 1mind are quote-based.


### My reps are drowning in basic qualification chats. What should handle them?


An AI website agent that qualifies against your ICP, answers routine product questions and only alerts a rep (or books a meeting) when a visitor clears your threshold. Start it on your highest-intent pages, connect it to your CRM's ownership rules, and review transcripts weekly to tune the threshold.
